follow_up.intent: Replace persisted process-local readiness epochs with restart-stable bounded encrypted-record revisions while retaining transient mutation checks and frozen-plan no-replay semantics.
follow_up.authorization: Root authorizes narrow SecretVault revision adapter and owned audit changes; no root worktree or remote mutations.
findings: ReadinessInvalidation.epoch resets on process start and cannot be persisted as configuration identity.
ToolConnectionRepository and SettingRepositoryImpl overwrite credentials under stable secret references; timestamps and references alone do not detect replacement.
SecretVault has no stable record revision API; a read-only encrypted-record digest can detect overwrites without hashing plaintext or creating/decrypting a key.
planned_tests: Same configuration after recreated services and changed process epoch remains admissible.
Same-reference credential and endpoint-secret overwrites block before dispatch.
Absent or unsupported record identities fail closed.
Concurrent snapshot/marker/read invalidation preserves no-dispatch or observed receipts.
Encrypted-record revision survives reopened vault, detects overwrite, rejects bounded malformed records and does not require or create a key.
changes: Persist only relevant saved configuration and opaque encrypted-record revisions; process-local epochs are never frozen as audit authority.
Keep an ephemeral generation guard from the start of inventory through dispatch and after reads, preserving observed receipts when authority changes.
Bind MCP auth/OAuth plus protected endpoint-query references, native credential and endpoint references, and the effective gateway credential with provider-owner consistency.
Return explicit PLUGIN_CREDENTIAL_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE when an identity is absent, unsupported, malformed or cannot be read; untracked plaintext credentials cannot be admitted.
Reuse existing vault framing limits and mutex. Revision inspection neither decrypts nor looks up or creates a key, and the allowlisted exporter still omits all fingerprints/revisions.

An OAuth refresh or same-value credential rewrite changes the encrypted record; a completed observation remains truthful and pending probes stop conservatively. Frozen plans are never rewritten or replayed.
